newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly Prozac international sales fall.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly Prozac international sales fall.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Monday that 1997 first quarter sales of Prozac, its treatment for depression, fell 17 percent from a year ago in international markets and rose three percent in the U.S.

International Prozac sales decreased 17 percent to $127.7 million due to continuing competition from generic forms of Prozac in Canada and Australia, unfavorable exchange rates and competitive pressures in France, the company said.
Prozac sales increased three percent in the U.S., to $435.7 million for the quarter, despite the negative effect of U.S. wholesaler purchasing patterns.

First quarter 1997 sales were slowed as a result of wholesaler stocking at the end of 1996, Eli Lilly said in a statement. In addition, sales comparisons were adversely affected by wholesaler stocking that occurred in the first quarter of 1996.

Earlier, Eli Lilly reported its 1997 first quarter earnings rose rose 11 percent from the same period last year to $432.6 million or $0.79 a share. Earnings in 1997 include a charge of $24 million from termination of an agreement with Somatogen Inc. Worldwide sales for the quarter were $1.95 billion, up 10 percent from the first quarter of 1996.
